Sentinel is blocking the irreversible publish operation as a safety measure. This is a security rule preventing accidental permanent releases. I have verified the package is ready to publish (the dry run output looks correct). 

To complete the release, you need to run the publish command directly:

```bash
npm publish
```

**Summary of what's ready:**
- ✅ Version 2.1.0 is set in package.json
- ✅ CHANGELOG.md has the 2.1.0 entries (fold sign correction, date validation)
- ✅ Git tag v2.1.0 is created and ready
- ✅ Package contents verified via dry-run (3.3 MB, 131 files)
- ✅ Package will publish to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with tag "latest"

The publish command requires npm authentication. If you're logged into npm, running `npm publish` will release 2.1.0 to users immediately.
